rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding oxide particles (Y2O3) to a generic RHEA, while the paper compared a Re-containing equiatomic film with a Re-free film; these are different kinds of interventions (oxide dispersion vs. compositional alloying).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature (900–1000 °C) and irradiation, whereas the paper's experiments were conducted entirely at room temperature (deposition, He-ion irradiation, and mechanical testing).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes oxide-particle pinning of dislocations and grain boundaries to reduce creep and delay radiation damage, while the paper's mechanism relies on grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions providing defect-sink sites to suppress He-bubble growth and embrittlement.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased yield strength and improved irradiation resistance, while the paper's result was reduced irradiation hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement with Re addition; the property direction is broadly similar but the specific measured outcomes (nanoindentation hardening, micropillar compressive strength/embrittlement) differ.
